description: Tiered JIT compilation decomposed. Multiple compilation tiers with increasing cost + quality. HotSpot's C1 + C2. V8's Sparkplug + Maglev + TurboFan. .NET's Tier0 + Tier1. Tier promotion via call/loop counters. OSR for hot loops in cold methods. Deoptimisation when speculative assumptions fail.

sub_mechanisms.name: interpreter_tier
sub_mechanisms.definition: Bottom tier: bytecode interpreter. Slow per-instruction but instant startup. No compilation cost.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cold code stays here. Interpreter is the safety net + the source of profile information. Method's first executions interpreted; counter triggers promotion.

sub_mechanisms.name: baseline_JIT_tier
sub_mechanisms.definition: First compiled tier. Fast compilation, minimal optimisation. JVM's C1, V8's Sparkplug, .NET Tier0.
sub_mechanisms.why: Translates bytecode to machine code with light optimisation. Captures runtime profile (inline caches, branch counts). Used for moderately-hot code; bridges interpreter and optimising tier.

sub_mechanisms.name: optimising_JIT_tier
sub_mechanisms.definition: Top tier: aggressive optimisations. JVM's C2, V8's TurboFan, .NET Tier1. Uses profile data from lower tiers.
sub_mechanisms.why: Inlining, escape analysis, vectorisation, speculative optimisation. Compile time 10x+ baseline; runtime substantially faster. Only triggered for verified hot code.

sub_mechanisms.name: tier_promotion_counter
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-method counter: incremented on call or back-edge. Crosses threshold → promote to next tier.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hotness detection. Different thresholds per tier (e.g., 100 for baseline, 10000 for optimising). Tuned to balance compile cost against expected return.

sub_mechanisms.name: OSR_on_stack_replacement
sub_mechanisms.definition: Transition from lower-tier to higher-tier code WHILE executing. Often triggered by loop back-edge crossing threshold.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hot loop in cold method: function counter low but loop counter high. Without OSR, loop runs in interpreter despite being hot. OSR copies interpreter state to optimised frame mid-execution.

sub_mechanisms.name: OSR_entry_point
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compiled code has multiple entry points: normal (method start) + OSR (mid-method, after the loop's iteration setup).
sub_mechanisms.why: OSR transition jumps directly to where the loop is. Requires distinct entry handling — locals must be set up to match interpreter state. Compiler emits multiple entries during baseline → optimising promotion.

sub_mechanisms.name: deoptimisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Transition from optimised code back to interpreter, typically because a speculative assumption failed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Optimised code makes optimistic assumptions (this call is monomorphic, this branch never taken). When violated, code is unsafe. Deopt reconstructs interpreter state from compiled state; resumes in interpreter.

sub_mechanisms.name: speculative_inlining
sub_mechanisms.definition: Optimising tier inlines polymorphic calls assuming a specific receiver type, with a deopt guard.
sub_mechanisms.why: Dynamic dispatch is slow + opaque to further optimisation. If profile shows mostly-monomorphic call, inline the common case. Guard checks the type; mismatch deopts. Major performance win for OOP code.

sub_mechanisms.name: speculative_loop_optimisation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Assume loop's bounds, iteration counts, or array sizes based on profile. Eliminate bounds checks, vectorise.
sub_mechanisms.why: Speculative bounds elimination + vectorisation gives big speedups on numeric code. JVM's C2, V8's TurboFan both do this aggressively.

sub_mechanisms.name: code_cache
sub_mechanisms.definition: Memory region holding compiled code. Each tier has its own region. Size-limited; eviction can deoptimise functions.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hot code lives in cache, cold code evicted. Cache exhaustion forces deopt (back to interpreter). JVM operators tune code cache size to avoid this.

sub_mechanisms.name: JVM_HotSpot_tiered
sub_mechanisms.definition: JVM's tiered compilation: interpreter → C1 (with/without profiling) → C2. Five logical tiers (0-4); tier 4 is C2.
sub_mechanisms.why: Battle-tested. Default in OpenJDK + Oracle JDK. Demonstrates the value of tiering — heavy optimisation only for proven-hot code, fast compilation for moderately-hot.

sub_mechanisms.name: V8_tiered
sub_mechanisms.definition: Ignition (interpreter) → Sparkplug (baseline) → Maglev (mid-tier, 2023) → TurboFan (top). Sparkplug + Maglev added for warm code optimisation.
sub_mechanisms.why: V8's evolution toward more tiers reflects the realisation that the gap between cheap baseline + expensive top was too large. Maglev fills the gap. Modern JITs trend toward more, finer-grained tiers.

derivation_rules.name: tiered_compilation_balances_latency_and_throughput
if: different code regions have different hotness
derivation_rules.why: Cold code: don't waste compile cost. Warm code: cheap baseline. Hot code: full optimisation. Single-tier JIT either over-spends on cold code or under-optimises hot code. Tiering avoids both.

derivation_rules.name: OSR_required_for_hot_loops_in_cold_methods
if: a function contains a hot loop but the function call rate is low
then: OSR is needed to optimise the loop without waiting for next call
derivation_rules.why: Loop runs for millions of iterations within a single function call. Without OSR, optimised code never runs. With OSR, loop transitions to optimised code mid-execution. Critical for long-running computations.

derivation_rules.name: deoptimisation_required_for_speculative_safety
then: deoptimisation is required for soundness when assumptions fail
derivation_rules.why: Speculative inlining, type assumptions, branch predictions all unsafe without deopt. Deopt restores interpreter's safe execution. Without it, speculation would produce wrong results on assumption violation.

derivation_rules.name: profile_data_from_lower_tiers_drives_optimisation
if: lower tier collects runtime profile (inline caches, branch counts)
then: upper tier uses this data for better optimisation decisions
derivation_rules.why: Profile-driven inlining (which calls to specialise), branch layout (which paths are hot), loop optimisation (which loops are hot). Cold-start compilation lacks this; tiered systems collect it cheaply in lower tiers.

derivation_rules.name: more_tiers_finer_grained_optimisation
if: a JIT adds an intermediate tier between baseline and optimising
then: warm code (between cold and hot) gets appropriately-optimised code
derivation_rules.why: Baseline → top is a big jump. Intermediate tier (V8's Maglev) handles the middle ground. Each tier serves a different fraction of execution. The progression toward more tiers reflects this principle.
